metadata.title: Bare Metal Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Defines foundational trust assumptions for non-virtualized physical compute substrates on which all higher-level platforms depend.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Applies to physical servers, firmware, provisioning systems, and out-of-band management planes.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Establishes explicit trust boundaries at the point where software execution meets physical hardware.

props.name: nist-control-family
props.remarks: Physical and environmental protection of compute substrates.

props.name: nist-control-family
props.remarks: Configuration management of hardware, firmware, and provisioning pipelines.

props.name: nist-control
props.remarks: Integrity verification of firmware and boot processes.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced for platform firmware resiliency guidance addressing BIOS, UEFI, BMC, and early-boot integrity, detection of compromise, and recovery to a known-good state. This pattern operationalizes those expectations at the hardware execution boundary.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced to establish bare-metal compute as a critical enabling dependency whose failure or compromise can cause cascading impact, requiring anticipatory protection and survivable recovery.

metadata.remarks: Bare Metal Core defines the trust baseline for physical compute hosts prior to virtualization, containerization, or cloud abstraction. This pattern exists to prevent implicit assumptions about hardware integrity, provisioning pipelines, and management control planes, and to make physical host trust an explicit, assertable capability.

components.title: Physical Host Integrity
components.description: Expectations for the integrity, inventory, and controlled lifecycle of physical compute hosts.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Insertion of compromised, counterfeit, or tampered physical hardware.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Authoritative inventory and lifecycle control of physical compute assets.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Physical hosts are inventoried and managed as controlled assets.
Physical access to compute hosts is restricted and monitored.

components.title: Firmware and Boot Trust
components.description: Trust assumptions for firmware integrity and early boot execution stages.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Persistence through compromised firmware or boot loaders.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Verification of firmware and boot integrity prior to workload execution.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Integrity checks on firmware and boot components.
Restricted changes to firmware and boot configuration.

components.title: Out-of-Band Management Trust
components.description: Trust and governance of out-of-band and remote management interfaces.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of valid management credentials to control hardware platforms.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Governing out-of-band interfaces as highly privileged control planes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Least privilege enforced for out-of-band management access.
Strong authentication required for privileged management interfaces.

components.title: Provisioning and Lifecycle Control
components.description: Trust in host provisioning, re-imaging, and decommissioning workflows.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Persistence or misconfiguration introduced through compromised provisioning pipelines.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Controlled, auditable provisioning and decommissioning workflows.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Standardized and approved baseline configurations for provisioning.
Formal change control over provisioning and lifecycle workflows.
